decision: Crash-after-commit fault injection applies only to authenticated mutating worker operations; authenticated read-only probes such as stats/get remain available.
problem: Dual-service qualification preflight probes the fault qrexec service with stats. With DIG_CRASH_AFTER_COMMIT=1 applied to every authenticated operation, the fault service exited after stats and could never pass preflight even when policy, authentication, topology, and storage were healthy.

reviewedApproaches.name: Skip fault-service preflight
reviewedApproaches.reason: Would defer discovery of a broken fault qrexec policy/service until a recovery campaign is already running.

reviewedApproaches.name: Create a separate health-only qrexec service
reviewedApproaches.reason: The health service would not prove that the actual fault service can authenticate and access the configured durable state, and it adds another policy/service surface.

reviewedApproaches.name: Scope crash injection to mutating operations
reviewedApproaches.reason: The synthetic fault hook models committed-response loss, which only has meaning after a state-changing operation. Read-only stats/get remain probeable while submit/claim/heartbeat/complete/fail still exercise the crash path.

added: fault-only qrexec service answers authenticated stats without exit 86
fault-only qrexec service still exits 86 after authenticated submit

failuresAndLessons: Fault injection controls must model the failure window precisely; broad hooks can invalidate health/readiness probes and create false blockers.
A preflight should exercise the exact service that later runs the campaign, not a substitute health endpoint.
Read-only control-plane probes must remain non-mutating and should not trigger committed-response-loss simulation.
safety: Synthetic defensive orchestration only; no real financial transactions or external side effects.
